question: Identify the artist with the highest overall sales of albums (tie broken by alphabetical order) and the artist with the lowest overall sales of albums (tie broken by alphabetical order), then calculate the amount each customer spent specifically on those two artists’ albums. Next, compute the average spending for the customers who purchased from the top-selling artist and the average spending for the customers who purchased from the lowest-selling artist, and finally return the absolute difference between these two averages.
sql:
WITH artist_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        a.ArtistId,
        a.Name AS artist_name,
        SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS total_sales
    FROM invoice_items ii
    JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
    JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
    JOIN artists a ON al.ArtistId = a.ArtistId
    GROUP BY a.ArtistId, a.Name
),
top_bottom AS (
    SELECT 
        MAX(CASE WHEN rn_asc = 1 THEN ArtistId END) AS top_artist_id,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rn_desc = 1 THEN ArtistId END) AS bottom_artist_id
    FROM (
        SELECT *,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_sales DESC, artist_name ASC) AS rn_asc,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_sales ASC, artist_name ASC) AS rn_desc
        FROM artist_sales
    )
),
avg_top AS (
    SELECT AVG(spending) AS avg_spending
    FROM (
        SELECT i.CustomerId, SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS spending
        FROM invoice_items ii
        JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
        JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
        JOIN artists a ON al.ArtistId = a.ArtistId
        JOIN invoices i ON ii.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
        WHERE a.ArtistId = (SELECT top_artist_id FROM top_bottom)
        GROUP BY i.CustomerId
    )
),
avg_bottom AS (
    SELECT AVG(spending) AS avg_spending
    FROM (
        SELECT i.CustomerId, SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS spending
        FROM invoice_items ii
        JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
        JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
        JOIN artists a ON al.ArtistId = a.ArtistId
        JOIN invoices i ON ii.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
        WHERE a.ArtistId = (SELECT bottom_artist_id FROM top_bottom)
        GROUP BY i.CustomerId
    )
)
SELECT ABS(a1.avg_spending - a2.avg_spending) AS absolute_difference
FROM avg_top AS a1
CROSS JOIN avg_bottom AS a2;

{"sql": "WITH artist_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        a.ArtistId,
        a.Name AS artist_name,
        SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS total_sales
    FROM invoice_items ii
    JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
    JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
    JOIN artists a ON al.ArtistId = a.ArtistId
    GROUP BY a.ArtistId, a.Name
),
top_artist AS (
    SELECT artist_name, ArtistId
    FROM artist_sales
    ORDER BY total_sales DESC, artist_name ASC
    LIMIT 1
),
bottom_artist AS (
    SELECT artist_name, ArtistId
    FROM artist_sales
    ORDER BY total_sales ASC, artist_name ASC
    LIMIT 1
),
customer_spending AS (
    SELECT 
        i.CustomerId,
        a.Name AS artist_name,
        a.ArtistId,
        SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS spending
    FROM invoice_items ii
    JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
    JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
    JOIN artists a ON al.ArtistId = a.ArtistId
    JOIN invoices i ON ii.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
    GROUP BY i.CustomerId, a.Name, a.ArtistId
)
SELECT 
    ta.artist_name AS top_artist,
    ba.artist_name AS bottom_artist,
    avg_top.avg_spending AS avg_top_spending,
    avg_bottom.avg_spending AS avg_bottom_spending,
    ABS(avg_top.avg_spending - avg_bottom.avg_spending) AS absolute_difference
FROM top_artist ta
JOIN bottom_artist ba ON 1=1

    SELECT CustomerId, AVG(spending) AS avg_spending
    FROM customer_spending
    WHERE ArtistId = (SELECT ArtistId FROM top_artist)
    GROUP BY CustomerId
) avg_top ON 1=1
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT CustomerId, AVG(spending) AS avg_spending
    FROM customer_spending
    WHERE ArtistId = (SELECT ArtistId FROM bottom_artist)
    GROUP BY CustomerId
) avg_bottom ON 1=1;"}
